clauses.reason: Item 1 designates March 31, 1954 as the dedication day for the Goethals memorial in the Canal Zone and lets the Governor arrange ceremonies. It covers that single day, so it ended by its own terms at the close of March 31, 1954. No later order is held that revokes, postpones or extends it.

Item 2 excuses federal officers and employees on the Isthmus of Panama from duty on March 31, 1954 and treats the day as a holiday there. It covers that single day, so it ended by its own terms at the close of March 31, 1954. Executive Order 10358, cited for the meaning of holiday, is an earlier order that does not reach it, and no later order is held that revokes, postpones or extends item 2.

research_rationale:
EO 10523 (signed 1954-03-26 by Dwight D. Eisenhower; filed 1954-03-29, 10:13 a.m.; 19 FR 1689, Federal Register of March 30, 1954 per the held source record) is read in full from the registered text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10523.txt; its number, title and date agree with the census register. Inventory: four recitals (the Goethals memorial authorized by Congress, the Commission's report that its work is complete, the anniversaries, and the wish to dedicate the memorial), which command nothing, and two numbered commands. Item 1 designates Wednesday, March 31, 1954 as the day for dedicating the memorial to Major General George W. Goethals in the Canal Zone and allows the Governor of the Canal Zone to arrange ceremonies. Item 2 excuses federal officers and employees on the Isthmus of Panama from duty on March 31, 1954, with the usual exceptions, and treats the day as a holiday on the Isthmus within the meaning of Executive Order 10358 and of the statutes on compensation and leave. First end: both items are limited to the single day March 31, 1954, so each was performed and spent at the close of that day. The text has no until-wording and no extension or renewal. Later instruments: EO 10358 (June 9, 1952; held as actor context and read) predates this order, is cited only for its definition of holiday and supersedes only EO 9636 (its section 8), so it cannot end this order; the dossier's missing line about EO 10358 and the one OFR-catalog hit concern that citation. A scan of every held order text for the bare number 10523 found only the order's own copy, the preceding order's text that prints the same issue contents, and unrelated page numbers. Machine searches adopted after reading their coverage notes: current-law:usc (U.S. Code release point 119-121, citations of the order by number, edition through 2026-10-09, no hit), current-law:ecfr (eCFR as of 2026-10-14 and GovInfo CFR bulk, citations by number, no hit) and later-events:ofr_catalog (Office of the Federal Register disposition notes for 1937 onward plus operative sentences of saved order texts).

savings.reason: The order has no savings, pending-matter or continuing-effect wording. The dedication ceremony and the excused duty were completed on March 31, 1954; pay and leave for the excused day follow the compensation and leave statutes and Executive Order 10358, which the order invokes but does not extend.
